utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. First, I have to admit that I'd forgotten to turn into open session yesterday before adjourning. That's the reason why we're now in open session, although we'll turn into closed session relatively soon. When we are waiting for the witness to be brought in, I have one or two short matters, but the Usher can already try to find him. What would the parties like to do with the handwritten letter we've seen yesterday? I can imagine that you -- it's available to you and that there's no need to further do anything with it. But before deciding on the matter -- that's the letter to VWS. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would ask that it be exhibited. And I believe the Chamber said yesterday that the Prosecution and Defence would be provided with copies of the reply to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that has not been done yet, then I think I would consult the VWS to see whether we just inform you about the content, which to some extent we've done already, or whether there's any reason why VWS considers any confidentiality in there. The Defence, do you think that the letter written to VWS should be an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I have the opportunity to go through it in detail, please? I didn't look at it overnight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we simply don't have a position. I don't see the point, but if any of the parties, including the Chamber, believe it might be helpful, let it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we in closed session? No, we're not yet in closed session. We turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in closed session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in closed session. The witness may be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There was a matter, but it can wait, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness JF-026, first of all, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you would speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would like to invite you to tell us whether there are any matters you found in the transcript of the first case and/or the transcript of the second case which you consider to be not in accordance with the truth, and to inform us about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, to the extent I was able to, I looked through the material from Case 1, and I have one observation to make which concerns page 180.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 180. Let's just -- yes, page 180 would translate into our page numbering how, Mr. Groome, if you would --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We cannot translate. That's the problem, the way it's been published. That's why if the witness could read and orient us that way, I think we may be able to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you could read one or two lines of the portion you want to draw our attention to, then we'll be able to find it. Witness, could you read a portion of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the penultimate paragraph on the page, where a time-frame has to be set. I am answering that it was because of the MUP of Serbia, because the Prosecutor asked me if this was -- if it was the person from the MUP of Serbia, and the year concerned was 1993, when the individual was not a member of the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would literally read one line, then we'll try to find it in the English. And so if you would read one line, and then -- well, let's say the first line of your answer, we'll then try to find it, and then you'll have an opportunity to further explain. Could you read that one line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It reads: "Prosecutor Groome. "Q. But the person you handed over your request to is a member of the MUP of Serbia?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "We didn't even know. We simply asked for assistance then, and my friend at the time, an employee of the MUP of Serbia ..." I think maybe this is the entry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the first case, I'm in the range of 21 --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: This is the 5th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 5th of June of the year ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, one second, one second. Okay, I'll now read it in context and see whether we are at the same page. Witness, I'll read the question, and perhaps you follow it: "So Arkan's appearance in Zvornik was after you made a request to the MUP of Serbia for assistance in Zvornik?" Then your answer was: "No, we were not in the MUP. We were at the Assembly Committee." Then the question was: "But the person you conveyed your request to was a member of the MUP of Serbia?" And then you said: "Yes, it is through him that I received information that after Bijeljina, Arkan would come to Zvornik." Is that the portion you're referring to? What would you like to change or to add?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, since this is about 1992, this individual was not a member of the MUP at the time. I said that I did not specify the time-frame. He was not a member of the MUP of Serbia at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, let's see. You say he was not a member of the MUP at that time. Did he become a member of the MUP after 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Based on the fact that I knew that he had been a member of the MUP, whether it was 1993 or 1994, I said that the individual was a member of the MUP. But I don't know the exact time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could tell us who it was. Then we have an opportunity to verify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's Kostic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's Rado Kostic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, that's now on the record. Are there any other portions which you consider not to be --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The rest that I reviewed, I think, reflects my evidence. But bear in mind that wherever I say that I directly participated in the events, that was the case, whereas in other portions where I do not make such a reference, I am probably inferring or conveying information I received from others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is no direct knowledge, but knowledge deriving from other sources. Now, is there any point where you have not personally observed what you describe? Is there any piece of information which you now say is incorrect? So it's clear that if you say, I observed this personally, then that's your own observation. It's also clear that if you do not say so, that you have obtained your information from other sources and cannot guarantee that it's correct. But is there anything you obtained from those other sources which you now say is certainly not correct or where you have serious doubts at this moment, despite you believed it was true when you told -- when you testified, that you now say, No, I know now, on the basis of additional information, that it is not true? Is there any such instance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not that I observed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave this for the time being. As far as other testimonies are concerned, I think the Prosecution did not tender the other material. You asked for it, Mr. Jordash, so we'll see what happens with that material, how you're going to use it, if you're going to use it at all. Mr. Petrovic, are you ready to continue? And could I also inquire as far as timing is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that I will need an hour and a half, so a bit more than a full session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, could you already give --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think I could finish by the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll see whether that's possible or not. If not -- if that would not be possible, the Chamber has already explored possibilities that if we couldn't finish today, that at least we could finish before the weekend. Of course, it would be appreciated if we do not need extra sessions, but just for you to know. Please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I have several questions for you. Tell me, the individual by the name of Milan Sojic, what role, if any, he had in the arming of the Serbian population of Zvornik in 1991 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Sojic hails from Zvornik. He held a high position in the National Bank of Serbia. It was through this capacity that he came to know certain JNA officers and was able to use certain channels to provide as much assistance as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that together with General Svetozar Andric, he procured weapons, that he was the contact?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time, General Svetozar Andric was captain first class and the chief of the military police for the town of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us -- generally speaking, can you tell us what the overall quantity of weapons that reached Zvornik originated from JNA sources, if you can?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, roughly 90 per cent from the JNA and 10 per cent from Baranja.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The 90 per cent you mention, it was distributed either directly from the JNA or through the SDS?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the most part from the JNA, and in part through the SDS. As I said, we manned their ranks, and as part of the instructions we were respond to the JNA call-ups as far as possible in order to fill up their reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, look at D49, please. It will appear on your screen shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'd like the witness to be shown page 3 in B/C/S and 4 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, these are conclusions and assessments of the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina which the Command of the 2nd District sent to the General Staff in March 1992. The document was compiled by and sent to the General Staff by Lieutenant General Milutin Kukanjac. I'd like you to look at item F, which is on page 289 of the photocopy. So under F, it reads, and it relates to the overall territory of Bosnia, that: "The JNA has distributed around 52.000, and the SDS around 17.000." What I'd like to know is whether this ratio that we see here can be roughly applied to the territory of Zvornik, which you have personal knowledge of?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, although I think that the ratio would be even higher in the direction of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you say "even higher," you mean that the higher amount of weaponry distributed by the JNA would apply to the territory of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'd stick by the 90 to 10 ratio, 90 per cent to 10 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 2D328, which 65 ter document, 2D328.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, would you be able to lay a foundation for this apparent judgement or assessment of the percentage, unless that's what you wanted to do with the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps there's a problem in interpretation. The witness said 90 per cent of the weapons came from the JNA. Then I showed him a document which related to the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and he told me that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no doubt about that. What I'd like to know is: What is the specific knowledge the witness has to say, overall, it may have been 75-25, but in Zvornik it was 90-10. And then to say, You were there, so you would know, is not a very strong basis for such a numerical assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was under the impression that I achieved as much through my line of questioning yesterday and today which related to the arming effort through the JNA. He referred to five or six sources which supplied the Zvornik area with weapons from the JNA. Let me ask him this:

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, based on your knowledge of the sources and quantities that we mentioned today and yesterday, can you ascertain that it was from the JNA that 90 per cent of the weapons arrived in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was on the basis of the assessments we made in the Crisis Staff to see to what extent certain areas were armed and to what extent certain areas were at risk, and that's how we made subsequent decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you keep a record of the numbers, and how and where they were distributed, and what their origin was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did keep records, as much as we could. I know the first time when the investigators put questions to me, they brought me at least 200 copies, and they showed me documents where I had personally signed for those distributions. We thought that there would not be a war, and we thought that there would be certain inspections that would ask, What happened with those weapons? As soon as the weapons were there, talks started about abuse, about smuggling, about illicit sales, and so on, and that's why we kept these records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The records would give an opportunity to verify the accuracy of the answers of the witness, so the parties are invited to consider that matter in a bit more detail. Please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, would you please look at the document that is on the screen in front of you, I believe. Please have a look at it. It's very brief. And then I'm going to put some questions to you. Have you had a look?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Are you, perhaps, familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that all the weapons that work organisations had were taken over by the JNA and the TO at one point in time in the beginning of the 1990s?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a well-known fact that the previous defence system was such that all work organisations had certain quantities of weaponry for TO purposes, and that was one of the sources of the conflict. We wanted them to be handed over to the JNA, and the Muslims wanted them to be handed over to the local TO, because in most municipalities they were in power.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Weapons were handed over to the TO. Do you know what happened afterwards to the weapons that were under JNA control in the coming period?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the JNA mobilised the reserve force, and quite a bit of this weaponry was distributed to those who had supported the JNA and united Yugoslavia, and for the most part those were the Serbs in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document please be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution does not object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D238 becomes Exhibit D152, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D152 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have 65 ter 00439, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It's a brief document. Could you please have a look, and then I'm going to put some questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you zoom in a bit? I cannot see it properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So the Public Security Station of the Serbian municipality of Skelani is requesting from the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of the Serb People in BiH -- this is a request for some equipment, actually. Tell me, since you headed the police station in Zvornik for a while, what about your Public Security Station; was this the route that you followed when you needed materiel and equipment or did you take a different course?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from the moment when Republika Srpska was established and from the moment when the JNA withdrew from the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, this was the way in which supplies were provided to the police. Up until then, we tried to make do in different ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Over here, they are asking that this request be forwarded to the federal SUP, so they are asking their ministry that the ministry ask the federal SUP for all of this. Was this the route that was taken, to the best of your knowledge, in the territory of your municipality as well?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. While the federal SUP was still in existence, that was standing practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: An inspector in the federal SUP, Zivorad Petrovic, is referred to here. Do you perhaps know the man?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document please be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit, although it is from the Prosecution 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've been able to verify the provenance and have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 3439 becomes Exhibit D153, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D153 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said to us, Witness, that Zuca and Marko Pavlovic were arrested at the same time. To the best of your knowledge, was the reason for the arrest of these two persons the same --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the question. The microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, could you repeat the last part of your question, since your microphone was switched off for the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. So the question is whether this witness knows whether these two persons were arrested at the same time and for the same reason, or does he not have any knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know they were arrested at the same time, but I don't know whether they were arrested for the same reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please have a look at -- 2846 is the Prosecution's 65 ter number. Could we please have a look at the first page of that document only. It's a very brief document. Please have a look at it. I'm sure that you've seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question is whether the volunteer units, including Zuca's unit in the territory of the municipality of Zvornik at the time, were financed by the provisional municipal authorities in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the first page of this document please be admitted? This document consists of several pages, but I think that only page 1 is relevant. It's another Prosecution document from their 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to the compound nature of the last question. The document refers to Zuca, and then the question was whether volunteer units, including Zuca. I would ask that both be explored with greater precision. With respect to the admission of this actual document, the Prosecution has verified its provenance and does not object to its admission now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think you can ask the question in re-examination, if you wish to do so. I asked for any objections. No objections. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first page of document 2846 becomes Exhibit D154, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D154 is admitted into evidence. Is there any need that this first page to be up-loaded separately from -- Mr. Petrovic, could you take care of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Prosecution believes that the Chamber should have the entire document before it is -- I'm sorry, but I wasn't clear about that before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any problem with the entire document, including the cover page, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, but I don't want to encumber you with facts that are of no great relevance for these proceedings. But if this is the Prosecutor's wish, I don't have a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the whole of the document is admitted. That's a 21-page document up-loaded in e-court. Please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, the provisional municipal authorities financed Zuca's unit; right?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We also have the Pivarski unit, then Gogic's unit. Were they also financed by the provisional municipal authorities?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the volunteer units were financed by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have a look at 2D332. This is a Defence document from the Defence 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at this document very briefly. First of all, tell us, please, whether you know of the Igor Markovic Unit. What is that?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a unit that was Zuca's unit until he got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, it's not very clear, who got killed, Zuca or Igor Markovic? Just tell us that.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Igor Markovic was killed, and then Zuca's unit was named after Igor Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Lieutenant-Colonel Vidoje Blagojevic is?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a man who was commander of the Zvornik Brigade for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, does this correspond to your knowledge as well, the content of this document, that is, that the army is providing fuel to Zuca's unit for their vehicles, the unit that was then called "Igor Markovic"?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of these volunteer units were placed under the command of the JNA and later under the command of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And then the JNA -- or, rather, the Army of Republika Srpska supplied them with materiel and other resources, including fuel, as we can see on the basis of this document as well?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document please be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm unable to verify the provenance of the document. I would ask it be marked for identification, and then we'll seek to speak with Mr. Petrovic during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, this document should be assigned an MFI number, which will be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D332 becomes Exhibit D155, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, if I understood your testimony correctly, your first contact and first request for assistance was addressed to Radmilo Bogdanovic and the Parliamentary Committee for Serbs Outside Serbia; right?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And Radmilo Bogdanovic was the person who told you to communicate with Radoslav Kostic; right?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what did you infer on that basis? What was the relationship between Bogdanovic and Kostic?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in view of the position that Bogdanovic had in the Assembly as an MP and as the head of the Committee for the Position of Serbs Outside Serbia, it was my understanding that they knew each other well and that they were on good terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue: The document which was MFI'd, that is, about the fuel, the translation is not only the page we find in the original, but the translation also deals with handwritten text on the back of the document. Now, that appears not, as far as I can see, in the original which is up-loaded, which is a one-page document. So, therefore, I'm wondering, where the translation covers more than the original, what you intend to do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my intention is to establish whether we can find the back of the original and then up-load all of that into e-court, and then we tender it. This is the only document that I found, but there must be this other page as well. I do apologise to everyone in the courtroom because of that. This was an oversight on my part. But I have no problem with the content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in 1991 and 1992, you knew that Radoslav Kostic was commander of the police station in Darda and Baranja.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him several times there in Darda. I even went to his home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that only in 1994 or 1995, you found out that Radoslav Kostic also worked in the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that sometime towards the end of the war. I don't know whether it was 1994 or 1995. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, this weaponry from Baranja, do you know who it belonged to, whose weapons these were?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were weapons of the JNA that they had left from the days of Yugoslavia; that is, the Territorial Defence of Baranja.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And during this period of time that you are talking about, these weapons belonged to the Army of the Republic of the Serb Krajina; right.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what sort of role was played by Marko Pavlovic in the territory of Baranja at a time when combat operations took place there.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he was the TO commander for the town of Darda or the town of Beli Manastir, I'm not sure, although I think it was Darda.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that around 300 pieces of weaponry had arrived from Baranja.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what sort of weapons these were?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will tell you now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I have marked as page 41, though I don't think that's the right pagination. I will find it as soon as I can. I don't think it will help you if I tell you that it's page 41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the Chamber was never provided with the testimony in the second case. So since we always very much appreciate to follow closely your questions, is there any way that you'd provide us with the relevant pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can be of assistance now and ask that 65 ter 5865 - that's the Prosecution's 65 ter document - be called, paragraph 40, the last two sentences of paragraph 40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we talking about the testimony in the second case or are we talking about the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are referring to the witness's statement. As for his evidence in the other case, I will have a look at that over the break. But he also refers to it in his statement. That's why I referred you to it. I will do my best to find it in the transcript as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, Mr. Petrovic, so that we are able to follow. Yes, a reference is made to 200 to 300 guns and ammunition. I found it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, it had to do with old M-48 rifles that were sent to you from Baranja; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, these were mostly dysfunctional weapons that we had to repair. They were outdated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can we be of assistance to the Trial Chamber? What sort of a rifle is an M-48, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the simplest form, and it's a make that's over 60 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mention is made in your statements of the lorry that was picked up from the parking-lot next to the Belgrade fair. When you went to pick up the truck, did you find anyone there?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't. We had agreed with Kostic that we should leave a lorry full of fuel and some flour, and that there would be individuals coming to pick it up in the afternoon. It is a great distance, after all, 300 kilometres from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As far as you know, they drove the lorry to Baranja, or were the weapons obtained from a different source, or you don't know.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know at the time. I know from the subsequent stories from individuals who loaded weapons. I have -- some of my employees, current employees, are from Baranja. So they went to Belgrade and then -- took the lorry there, and then went for the load to Baranja, to Darda.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now go back to the early days of the conflict in your town.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because of the tense situation - the Muslims had taken over the entire Zvornik, including the police station - we left the station and went in the direction of Karakaj. This was one of the instructions which had to do with the Cutileiro Plan that had been signed by Karadzic, Izetbegovic, and I think it was Mate Boban on behalf of the Croats, whereby the police force in the BH was supposed to be divided. Then we received a dispatch from the assistant minister of the interior, Momcilo Mandic, who was the highest-ranking Serbian in the Ministry of the Interior of the Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When they took over the police station, did the Muslim members of the police force distribute any weapons, and to whom, if they did.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. We went to see them on a couple of occasions later on, because we wanted to negotiate, and then we realised that they had distributed all of the weapons that belonged to the reserve force, I think it was around 400 pieces of weaponry. They had even recruited criminals who had been serving long-term sentences. They dressed them in uniforms and formed a reserve force out of them overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When the Muslims took over the police station, what became of the Serbian population in the town of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the time the Serbs had left Zvornik, they were either in the surrounding Serbian villages or in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I'd like to ask you about the role of the JNA at the time. Yesterday, you told us that there was a number of strategically-important locations of the JNA in the municipality of Zvornik; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As the JNA grew out into the Army of Yugoslavia, did the locations carry the same significance as before, in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA was present there until the time when the VRS was formed, at which point the VRS took over their role. I think it was on the 28th of May or June. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I was asking you specifically about the locations we referred to, the hydroelectric plant in Zvornik, the bridges there. Were these locations protected by, initially, the JNA, and then later on by the VRS, because of their strategic importance?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that when the JNA withdrew, some of the units of the VJ took part in the actions in the municipality of Zvornik, such as, for instance, the unit from Valjevo, under the command of Solaja, and some other units.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know of this one instance which involved the unit from Valjevo. I know about this because we, as the Executive Board, which I was a functionary of at the time, paid them a reimbursement for -- or some sort of a salary for one month. When that was, exactly, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown Prosecution 65 ter 4012.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I -- perhaps, when waiting for this, could you give us the name of one of the criminals which you say were dressed in uniforms? Could you give us one example of such a criminal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Behluli. I don't know his last name. He was one of the well-known criminals. Then Musadik Halilovic. I don't remember, given the time that has elapsed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's the basis for your information that they are criminals? Are you aware of any convictions or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: station, and I know for a fact that they had been convicted for serious crimes, such as murder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. One other question. You were talking about the take-over of the police station, but you also referred to the take-over of the whole of Zvornik. Could you tell us exactly what you meant by that? Was that a take-over of Zvornik by force, or what exactly did you mean when you said that Zvornik was taken over, including the police station.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because of the political divisions that existed at the time, as soon as the Muslims took over the police station, the Serbs did not feel secure there and simply left Zvornik. Thus, it was solely Muslims who stayed behind in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what you're referring to is that when the police station was taken over, that the Serbs then left, so that there was no specific combat or armed conflict, it's the result of taking over the police station that the Serbs left, and that's what you refer to as the take-over of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We withdrew to the neighbouring place called Karakaj, which had a Serb majority. We set up a police station there, and the Serbian population followed suit. They also left Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, therefore, entire Zvornik means the town of Zvornik; is that not the whole of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the town, not the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please have a look at the document. It's a document issued by the Command of the 1st Military District, whereby the OG Drina is ordered to secure all the facilities on the two banks of the Drina River all the way to the River Sava, excluding Bijeljina, Modranj village, Vitnica village, et cetera. Tell us, do the contents of this order reflect what you, yourself, were able to see; i.e., that the JNA or the VJ secured the strategic locations along the length of the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can the document be exhibited as -- be admitted as a Defence exhibit? It is a Prosecution 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 4012 becomes Exhibit D156, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D156 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'd now like to ask you about Marko Pavlovic, i.e., Branko Popovic. Tell us, first, on what sort of terms was Pavlovic with members of the JNA, primarily officers, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I concluded, based on my acquaintance with him, was that he was on excellent terms, friendly terms, with some of the most senior officers, including generals.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- can you give us an illustration?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that he was on excellent terms with General Jankovic, who was the commander of the Tuzla Corps, and with some other generals who were on the General Staff, whose names I can't recall at present. I know that I was present on a couple of occasions when he was engaged in telephone conversations with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about his relationship with Colonel -- do you know about his relationship between Pavlovic and General Dubajic?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I know that they did have an excellent relationship and they would socialise with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So he had excellent -- an excellent relationship with General Jankovic, who was the commander of the Tuzla Corps, and with Dubajic, who was his chief of security?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At some point in one of your statements, I also read that Pavlovic was on excellent terms with the chief of the General Staff, Panic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. At least that's how he represented things. He would boast about it. And I did see them together on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if Pavlovic turned to these senior officers for assistance, either in materiel or in combat assistance?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the case before the conflicts broke out, when he requested to be given a materiel assistance, and when the fighting broke out, when he would ask for assistance in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Pavlovic at any point in time contact any of these officers in your presence?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do seem to recall that we were in the Crisis Staff at some point when he placed a telephone call. It had to do with materiel and equipment which subsequently arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Marko Pavlovic ever call anyone from the MUP of the Republic of Serbia or any other service of the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that sort of knowledge. He stayed in Zvornik for a while. We socialised privately. We knew the man who was from across the street, the commander of the station and a person from Loznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did he call anyone from the DB of Serbia in your presence?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at 2D329. It is a certificate of gratitude issued to Branislav Pavlovic for exceptional commitment, dedication and co-operation in offering assistance to soldiers, TO members and the Serbian people exposed to Ustasha terror and genocide, for the Military Post 5055, Colonel Radoslav Blazic. The date is the 25th of March, 1992. Is this certificate consistent with what you knew of the relationship Pavlovic had with the JNA at the time?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at P1063, page 5. I'm sorry, page 6, please. Page 6, section VII, Roman numeral VII. Further, a bit further, please. One page ahead in B/C/S, please. In e-court, it is page 8. Sorry, page 9. I would just like to establish a parallel with the previous document. I'm sorry that this has taken a while. So number 26 says: "The command of the defence of the city of Belgrade is Military Post Code 5055."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wanted to show you -- or, rather, I wanted us to identify the military post code. Excuse me. It seems that there is no English translation of this document. The document has not been translated in full, apparently. It is a Prosecution document, and, therefore, I am so surprised that that is the case. However, I wanted to indicate what can be seen here in the Serbian version. It's a Prosecution document, a Theunens document. We are going to up-load the entire translation that we are going to ask for.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please read point 26 for us? And we are going to present it in an appropriate manner to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The command of the defence of the city of Belgrade, 5055, Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document 2D329 which I showed a few moments ago, that certificate of gratitude, could it please be admitted as a Defence exhibit? As for this document, we are going to supply the missing translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first have a look at the previous document you referred to. Could we have it on the screen again; that is, the certificate of gratitude. Yes. If I look at the transcript, Mr. Petrovic, you said: "I'd like to ask you about Marko Pavlovic, i.e., Branko Popovic." Now, this document is about Branislav Pavlovic, which does not fit with either of the two names you gave us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that the only explanation I can offer is the following: He used the names Pavlovic, Popovic, Branko, Marko, alternately, so it must be a combination of those two names. However, we can investigate that. So could it please be marked for identification before we've looked into the matter and before we're in a position to give you an explanation? Then it's more appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could be of assistance. The same thing occurred to me, I'd never seen the combination of the first and the second name. But when we checked the provenance of it, we find that it was given to the Office of the Prosecutor by Branko Popovic in an interview with an investigator of the OTP on the 12th of March, 2003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was given by Branko -- by whom exactly did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, the person -- the two names that I have heard this person use is "Marko Pavlovic" and "Branko Popovic." Just one second, Your Honour. The name that he represented as his name to the investigator who interviewed him was "Branislav Pavlovic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So "Branko," is that short for Branislav," or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It is not exactly the usual thing, but yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we now have three first names and two family names, and we find a combination of all of it, and handwritten portions not being translated. No objections, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, this --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 2D329 becomes Exhibit D157, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D157 is admitted into evidence. I add to this that there was no objection from the Prosecution. Nevertheless, in evaluating the document, of course, we cannot just ignore that there is still a bit of unexplained background of this document and that not all of the handwritten text - I've got no idea what it is - is translated. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe that this would be the right time for the break, so I suggest that we do take the planned break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, I'd like to take you back to P1063, which was admitted into evidence, but apparently without a full translation. I blame myself for not having noticed that at the time, but sometime I expect the parties to do that first. I suggest that it will be re-MFI'd until we have a full translation, even if that would not be a copy of all the names, because I saw there were long lists, but that at least that it's clear what these lists are and that it's not just one page translated and other pages not. That seems not to be an appropriate way of dealing with these kind of documents. Again, the Chamber is not insisting at this moment on every single name and long lists to be re-typed by interpreters, but at least it should be a clear coverage, in the English language, of the whole of the document. P1063 is, therefore -- the status of the document is changed and marked for identification. Mr. Groome, when will we hear from you on P1063?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, after the break, if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether you have a translation already by then, but, yes, we would like to. Then we'll take a break, and we'll resume at 10 minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber was informed that P1063 needs further attention before it can be admitted again. Mr. Petrovic, are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I would just like to point something out in relation to P1063; that it was a document that was used when witness -- expert witness Theunens testified, and the Prosecution pointed out that they had translated only those portions which are of relevance to them. So that is the core of the matter. We are going to resolve it, so I want to make it clear at this point as well. Thank you, Your Honour. I'm going to continue now. Could we please have P1394 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, would you please look at this document - it's very brief - and tell me whether you know who Slobodan Vasilic is?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Commander Vasilic was commander of the Zvornik Brigade after Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It says here that Marko Pavlovic is deployed in the Serbian Army?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The document bears the date of the 22nd of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The facts from this document, do they correspond to what you knew about Marko Pavlovic's position and deployment at the relevant time?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that Biljana Plavsic was in Zvornik a few days before the conflict, a day or two before the conflict?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that a meeting was held with her, it was a meeting of the Crisis Staff and the municipal leadership with her, and that you attended part of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear Plavsic ask at that meeting to have Arkan called to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you know at that point in time about the relationship between Arkan and Plavsic?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At this meeting with Plavsic before the conflict, was Peja in attendance as well?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Kostic conveyed information to you to the effect that Arkan was in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Kostic had not told you or ordered you to communicate with Arkan, he simply conveyed to you the information that Arkan was in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we called this Parliamentary Committee for Serbs Outside Serbia, and they instructed us to get in touch with Kostic. Kostic told us that it was best for us to try to contact Arkan because he was in Bijeljina, and perhaps he could help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Kostic told you several times --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that Kostic told you very bad things about Arkan several times?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: any dealings with Arkan, that one should stay away from Arkan?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said very, very bad things about him and his volunteer guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you came to Bijeljina, did you have the impression that it had already been agreed somewhere that Arkan was supposed to go to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I informed him about the situation in Zvornik, and he said that this Pejic, this associate of his, would go to Zvornik along with some 20 men. Now, whether that had been planned at a higher level, that is something I cannot claim with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So it is possible that Arkan came to Zvornik on the basis of your request? I mean, I'm not saying that it's your personal request. It was the request of the Crisis Staff, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is that that is what tipped the scales. Because the situation in Zvornik changed from one hour to the other, he was not aware of it. I told him about it, and I don't think that he could have had a plan from earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Plavsic come after the take-over of power in the town of Zvornik, itself?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You testified at some point that that is where she encountered Pejic and greeted him. What did this meeting between the two of them look like when they first met?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "You testified at some point" -- could you please allow the Chamber to follow what you're putting to the witness, that is?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because earlier I had to establish that when you referred to testimony, you were referring to testimony which was not in evidence. Then you used the statement of the witness and introduced a certain matter, which may appear in the testimony, which is not in evidence but which at that time did not appear in the statement, so we'd like to follow it very closely. Could you tell us what "at some point" means here?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will -- actually, I'll give you all the references. I hesitate in doing so, because I don't know what the fate of the previous testimonies is going to be. First of all, as for Kostic's opinion about Arkan, it is page 15033 in the testimony in Case number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We don't have that. You should be aware of that. I mean, we just haven't got it. No party tendered it. The only reason why we know it's there, because Mr. Jordash asked it to be provided to the witness to review it. But we want to follow the testimony in all details, so references to the testimony in the second case, unless you give us those pages, doesn't assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, from Case 2, 65 ter

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first ask Madam Registrar to make a print-out, a hard copy, of the page Mr. Petrovic is referring to. Yes, the first case, there we have the hard copies.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Case 1, encounter between Pejic and Plavsic after the take-over of the town, page 45 in e-court. I think that the Prosecution up-loaded the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The testimony has received what exhibit number, so that I can find it on my computer?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, still -- I see she's still busy in doing what you should have done, Mr. Petrovic; that is, giving us a hard copy of the relevant page from the second case. Now, for the first case, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the 65 ter was 5870.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No number has been pre-assigned yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not certain, but I can't recall that one has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then let me see whether I, nevertheless, should be able to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Those of us with hard copies, we would appreciate the transcript page, if Mr. Petrovic could provide that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 5870, page 45 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's not released in any way, then the Judges have no access to 65 ter numbers, and that's rightly so because we are supposed to look at the evidence, not at the total series of up-loaded documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I assist you with the page number, Your Honour, in Case 2; I mean, the page of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay, now we have hard copies. Please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, what was the manner of the greetings exchanged between Plavsic and Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was cordial, and they kissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what precisely is Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a neighbourhood on an elevation, and it is part of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the strategic importance of Kula Grad is for the town of Zvornik and the area?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's an area overlooking the rest of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown 65 ter 2D276.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, have you had a look at the document?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, this is an order issued by Savo Jankovic, major general, commander of the 17th Tuzla Corps?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if JNA units participated in the activities aimed at capturing Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did JNA units fire from artillery weapons from this bank of the Drina as part of the activities to seize Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was artillery fire, but I don't know the direction it came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who did the artillery belong to?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA, the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my colleague has just reminded me that we tendered this document on the list of documents we produced in relation to Expert Witness Theunens, so there's no need for me to tender it again, since it was discussed at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Perhaps it's important for Madam Registrar to know that this is dealt with again, that we have revisited this document today. That's in the internal systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can the witness be shown 65 ter 2D330.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to leap up but I just noticed Your Honour looking at the time: Perhaps, for Your Honours' information, I think there's a general agreement we're not going to finish today. Mr. Groome would like to have half an hour, and I think with having to try to deal with admissibility of the Case number 2 transcripts and with the cross-examination I'd like to do, I think it's extremely unlikely that we'd finish today. So I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that the Chamber will do everything to have an extra session tomorrow morning at 9.00. Just for the parties to know, Madam Registrar, if you could convey this message to CLSS. We were already informed that practicalities would not oppose against having an extra session tomorrow morning. At the same time, Mr. Petrovic, you gave us now the sources. You did ask the witness one question, whether he was warned against Arkan and that, You shouldn't have any business with him. I mean, if you put that question to the witness, it's totally irrelevant to point at another place where the witness said the same thing. If you just had asked the witness, without referring to any earlier testimony, then we would have saved five to ten minutes and a lot of efforts, which finally result in knowing that he said the same in the other case. So one and the same. You asked questions about how Pejic greeted Mrs. Plavsic. There, again, what's the use of referring to evidence we do not have, and then we have to ask -- since you're referring to it, then we have to look at it, and then the only thing to find is that there were warm greetings and that they embraced each other. If you would not have referred to any of the earlier evidence at some point, then the whole problem would not have been there. But as soon as you start referring to other material, please be aware that if the Chamber hasn't it available, it will take care that it will be available, at quite some expense of efforts, and totally unnecessary. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I fully accept your criticism, and I will make sure that I proceed differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please have a look at the document. It's a daily report of the Operational Centre of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the SFRY for the day of the 12th of April. Please look at the first two paragraphs only. Therein, losses are listed, losses, apparently, of "own forces," that's what it would appear, and it reads losses of two members of Arkan's men, a member of the TO, whereas, actually -- so three members of the Arkan's group were killed and one TO member and one lady doctor were wounded. As far as you remember, the Arkan's group acted as part of the JNA, in other words, as part of the Armed Forces of the SFRY in this period that we're referring to, 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I tender this document into evidence and wish that it be admitted as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document was received from the Government of Serbia. The Prosecution has no objection. We are unsure whether it is the subject of an application for protective measures. We believe it is not, but cannot verify that at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we provisionally put it under seal. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 2D330 becomes Exhibit D158, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D158 is admitted under seal. And, Mr. Groome, you're invited within the next five days to inform the Chamber, through the Registrar, whether the document needs to be under seal or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, have you heard of the case involving four individuals who were arrested in Zvornik shortly before the outbreak of hostilities?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who these four individuals were?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it involved Zuco, his brother Legija, and another dentist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the individual by the name of Fadil Mujic?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fadil Mujic was a colleague of mine in the SUP. He was the head of the Crime Department within the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, page 10, "Arrest of four Serbs," paragraph 54, a chief of the Criminal police department was Fadil Mujic. What's the use of asking this again? Are you aware of the arrest of four Serbs, that covers a whole of a paragraph. Why not focus on what you want to know in addition, because apparently you are happy with the answer that Fadil Mujic was the chief of the Criminal Police Department? So why ask again?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Your Honour, because I don't know what the fate of these documents will be. We have challenged the documents and the way in which they were drafted, as well as the approach taken through 92 ter, but these are only two introductory questions that I put. I have two or three more questions, and I will finish then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What the fate will be of the 92 ter application depends on what is shown during the remainder of the cross-examination. Now, asking questions and being satisfied with exactly the same answers as we find in a document might earlier -- might, rather, support a 92 ter application than challenge such an application. Could you please try to limit the number of introductory questions, unless they are really necessary. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did Mujic tell you that he received two phone calls from Colonel Boskovic from Belgrade on the issue of these four arrested individuals?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you that Colonel Boskovic said that two of the four arrested were military policemen?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Mujic tell you that General Jankovic from Tuzla also called him with a request that the two individuals be released?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were both of them, Colonel Boskovic and General Jankovic, only interested in this individual, Bogdanovic, and Legija?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were interested in all four of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were these individuals at some point released from detention in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Colonel Boskovic was?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that he was a senior officer of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is that Nedeljko Boskovic, who was the senior officer of the Security Service of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did read in newspapers that Nedeljko Boskovic was a senior officer of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you about Vojislav Jekic. Did this person go around telling everyone that he was a member of State Security?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a very bad opinion of him, and the man is deceased. Well, he's the worst sort of person I ever met. He was the sort of person who would go around -- his tombstone is destroyed every week, so can I tell you anything more than that? It happens only to the worst possible people?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, why do you think that this is the worst person you met in your life?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He hails from Zvornik, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why not get an answer to your first question, Mr. Petrovic? Your answer was -- your question was: "Did Vojislav Jekic go around telling everyone that he was a member of the State Security?" That was the question, and I wouldn't mind to receive an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seemed to me, Your Honour, that I had heard the answer in B/C/S, but now I see that it's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did go around saying that he was a member of the State Security of Serbia, an official of the State Security of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us now, very briefly, what your response to the second question would be, in relation to your opinion about Jekic?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He hails from Zvornik, and he appeared when the war started. However, very soon we found out that he was just a wheeling-dealing sort of person. I don't know what the right medical term would be for this, but he obsesses. I think that you can check this with other people, but whatever this man ever said was a lie. Otherwise, this is my personal opinion, but everybody in Zvornik thinks that he is a very, very bad person. He pursued his personal interests, and he was prepared to do anything for the sake of those personal interests.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I would just like to go back to something, a question that I omitted, the action concerning Kula Grad. Do you know that JNA Officer Stupar, with his soldiers from the 72nd Brigade, also participated in the activities that had to do with the taking of Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that you only know of Franko Simatovic, Frenki, from the media?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, when the Judge cautioned me about these people, I never saw these people before. I have never seen them in my life before this, and so I was interested in seeing them. I saw Mr. Stanisic a few times in the newspapers, but I never saw this other gentleman's photograph, even. So then perhaps I was a bit too interested yesterday, and that's why I was looking at him so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On that basis, I conclude that you know nothing about the role of Franko Simatovic, Frenki, with regard to developments in Zvornik or anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first heard of him when the indictment was issued against him, and that's when I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. Just a moment, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when the town of Zvornik was taken, was there a small celebration that took place of any kind?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether that celebration was attended by Colonel Milosevic, the then-commander of the JNA from Romanija?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Arkan attend the celebration?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Jordash, are you ready to --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. If I may just get the lectern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the furniture has to be moved. Nowadays, it's plug-and-play, but the plug-in seems to be not easy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think we'll use the old microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I quickly ask you about a subject which, in some ways, comes before I get to the substance of your evidence. Is it right that after the end of the war, the Kula video of the centre involving the group the Red Berets was played very frequently on the TV in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And when I say "frequently," I mean hundreds of times. It was something that the population of Serbia were able to watch hundreds of times?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that we be a bit more specific after the time-frame? "After the war" includes all the way up to today and is a rather extensive period.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you recall when you first watched the video or the programme?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I know that it was broadcast on TV very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Would it have been in the late 1990s, early 2000?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that would be right, but I really do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you watch it before you actually spoke to the Prosecution, before your involvement with the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the answer would be, Yes, but I'm not sure. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I try to trigger your memory. Was it in the news in 2002?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I think that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that when you were interviewed by the Prosecution, you had, in your possession, many facts which came from the watching of that video?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that many of your ex-colleagues, colleagues from the time of the event in Zvornik and so on, would also have been in possession of those facts derived from the video?

utterances.speaker: JF-026 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
